newsitem.title: USA: Apple reluctant to share technology - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Apple reluctant to share technology - WSJ.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc will not withhold its latest available technology from Macintosh cloners, although it seems increasingly reluctant to share future advances, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday.

The paper said in its electronic edition that Apple reached a pact last week with one of its cloners -- Umax Computer Corp -- allowing Umax to use the latest version of the Macintosh operating system, the Mac OS 8.
The pact is to include other major cloners as well, the paper added.

The company, however, has not yet committed to licensing its next-generation operating system -- called Rhapsody -- or software the cloners need to start making Mac-compatibles using a new hardware design called the Common Reference Hardware Platform, the paper said.
A person close to Apple said the company wanted to curtail the cloners' success in winning Apple's sales of its most powerful Macintoshes, the paper reported.
Apple shares closed Friday up 1 11/16 at 19 3/16.
